August 2012 ## **20****th** **August – 31****st** **August** # Domestic supply on the rise CNIA reported that China produced 142,492 tonnes of copper-in-concentrate in July. Year-to-date output totalled 875,975 tonnes, representing an increase of 12.3% compared to the first seven months of 2011. Recently, two large mines have come on-stream. the Duobaoshan copper mine, based in Heilongjiang, was commissioned with a capacity of 30,000 tpy. The other major addition to output occurred this month, and resulted from the Phase II expansion of the Wunugetushan Copper mine, which added another 60,000 tpy of capacity. The increased supply of domestic copper concentrate has eased the raw materials balance within China, and this, together with the commitment by the China Smelter Purchasing Team to set a lower limit for terms of $50/5.0¢, has meant that the spot TC/RCs for imported concentrate rose to $50/5 from $40/4 last month. Given these new additions to output, China’s domestic mines are expected to produce roughly 1.4 million tonnes of copper-in-concentrate this year. Although CRU estimates that domestic mine production could rise by another 100,000 tonnes in 2013, Chinese mine output will fall well short of demand requirements, which for 2012 are expected to total 8.1 million tonnes of cathode. © 2012 CRU International Limited **confidential** **August 2012** www.crugroup.com # Tighter scrap market supports spot prices CNIA also reported that refined copper production reached 458,000 tonnes in July. Year-to-date, cathode output has amounted to just over 3.2 million tonnes, an increase of 8.9% compared with the same timeframe in 2011. Almost 1.1 million tonnes of scrap have been used in cathode production, slightly more than last year. China has been able to import 2.65 million tonnes of copper scrap so far this year, exceeding the 2.63 million tonnes delivered during the first seven months of 2011. Nevertheless, smelters are reportedly having difficulty sourcing secondary material. CRU understands that, since June, some facilities have cut production or closed for maintenance work. One refinery in Shandong, which has a capacity of 400,000 tpy, plans to close for maintenance for a full month in October. Given this lower scrap availability and expected maintenance shutdowns, CRU expects refined copper production to remain flat, or to fall slightly, during the rest of the year. This tightness in scrap supply helps to explain why spot market prices have moved higher over the last two weeks, despite the fact that stocks have risen. The chart above and to the left illustrates that the SHMET spot market, SHFE cash, and SHFE 3-month prices have all moved higher. In addition, the spread between the spot market price and the SHFE cash price has been positive since 16th August. The spot market price rose as high as RMB56,300/t on August 23rd , coinciding with a peak in the LME cash price. Since then, however, the spot price has declined, and was quoted at RMB55,900/t on August 29th . The LME cash price has moved in a tight range recently, with official settlement prices ranging from a low of $7,432/t on 20th August, to a high of $7,667/t on 23rd August. A lack of investor interest in copper, and in commodities overall, has reduced price volatility, as speculators wait to see how the Fed and the ECB respond in the coming months. While the SHFE/LME arbitrage has turned slightly positive, the Chinese domestic market is currently well supplied with cathode. The Flash PMI from HSBC/Markit for August indicated that Chinese export orders are set to contract, which means that manufacturing output is not likely to gather significant momentum during the next few months. Thus, the cathode that is already available to China in its © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 3 **August 2012** www.crugroup.com domestic warehouses, along with that and in nearby LME locations, should be adequate to meet any short-term uptick in demand, rather than require imports beyond what has already been contracted for the rest of this year. The range of quotations reported for imported cathode has narrowed to between $55/t and $65/t, as compared with the $40/t to $70/t range we published in the last _Fortnightly._ As a result, the average spot premium for imported cathode has risen slightly, to $60/t, compared to the prior $55/t. The premium for SXEW cathode has also increased, and was quoted at $50/t, versus the $40/t we reported in the last _Fortnightly_ . ### **Questions or comments may be addressed to:** **Wan Ling (Beijing):** +86 10 6510 2183 ling.wan@crugroup.com **James Wright (London):** +44 20 7903 2052 james.wright@crugroup.com This issue was completed on 31st August 2012.
